rules.title: Selected weakI systems
rules.rule: Present -e/-st/-ð/-að with selected contractions; past -e/-est/-e/-on added to the checked dental past stem. Long vowel+d gives dd in fēdde, scrȳdde, tōgelǣdde. Scęnc- takes -te, forwiern- -de.
rules.variants: Cook permits tt/t contraction. BT explicitly attests fēt/fētt/fēdeð; selected production target fēt. Uncontracted and alternative spelling forms are not independently new recall targets.
rules.boundary: Only declared indicative cells and separately listed complete command pairs; citations are supplied, not automatic infinitive production.

rules.title: Selected weakII systems
rules.rule: -ie, -ast, -að, plural -iað; preterite -ode, -odest, -ode, plural -odon. Command genēosa/genēosiað. Retain Cook longē in genēos-.
rules.variants: Cook records plural -edon beside -odon, ig(e)/g beside i in endings, and alternate past vowels; -odon and i are the selected productive forms. Alternative weakI andswerian remains unassigned.
rules.boundary: No regular weakII rule licenses another verb’s lexical case frame.

rules.title: Gewītan strongI
rules.rule: ī present, ā first/third singular past, short i second singular/plural past; t-stem contractions yield gewītst/gewīt. Select gewāt/gewite/gewiton.
rules.variants: Final tt beside t is source-rule supported; selected short t. Optional reflexive dative is attested, not obligatory in the chosen departure frame.
rules.boundary: Do not confuse with gewitan know.

rules.title: Supported unnan system
rules.rule: Indicative ann/unnon; past ūðe/ūðest/ūðe/ūðon; subjunctive unne/unnen and ūðe/ūðen, all persons. Present indicative2sg visibly has no assigned form. Direct addressed command uses second-person unne/unnen.
rules.variants: Cook an(n) permits an and ann; selected ann. Cook labels unne imperative; Fulk describes subjunctive substitution. Both source descriptions are preserved.
rules.boundary: No invented anst/unnest/unne indicative2sg or unnað formal imperative. The omission records checked-source limits, not universal nonattestation.

rules.title: Two bounded experiencer systems
rules.rule: Hyngreð/hyngrede with accusative experiencer and no expressed nominative; ðyncð/ðūhte with dative experiencer and a singular neuter nominative stimulus. Each defined finite system has exactly present3sg and past3sg.
rules.variants: Other personal and case frames are documented but not assigned; source quantity/spelling is explicit.
rules.boundary: No fabricated personal paradigm for the subjectless frame; no promotion of Unit9 entire passive/judgment construction.

rules.title: Case form and contextual role
rules.rule: Se has masculine/neuter singular ðȳ (variant ðon); strong gōd has gōde in those cells. Nouns, feminine singular and plural express this relation with dative-shaped forms. The food noun retains mete-dat-sg canonical identity; context marks instrumental function.
rules.variants: Prose mid+DAT ordinary; bare means more characteristic of poetry. Do not assign Anglian mid+distinct instrumental as the normal EWS production choice.
rules.boundary: All six newly promoted distinct cells are displayed; earlier ðes/hwā instruments remain recognition-only.

rules.title: u10-fedan-commands
rules.rule: Both singular and plural commands of fēdan.

rules.title: u10-scrydan-commands
rules.rule: Both singular and plural commands of scrȳdan.

rules.title: u10-geneosian-commands
rules.rule: Both singular and plural commands of genēosian.

rules.title: u10-wyrcean-commands
rules.rule: Both singular and plural commands of wyrcean.

rules.title: u10-genitive-relations
rules.rule: Bounded adnominal genitive: possession/kinship, origin or belonging, and the agent or object relation to a verbal noun; the dependent genitive retains its own case inside an externally governed head phrase.
rules.boundary: Cook §153d incorrectly names ęgesan rather than Frēan as objective genitive; preserve the printed text and correct the analysis.

rules.title: u10-genitive-quality-source
rules.rule: Recognize source setle his mægenðrymnesse: genitive of quality, naturally throne of his glory.
rules.boundary: Source-bound quality construction, not independent free productive abstract-genitive composition.

rules.title: u10-partitive-group
rules.rule: Substantival ān, sum and hwilc may select a genitive count group; the group stays genitive while the head has the case required by its clause.
rules.boundary: Contrast attributive ān agreeing with a singular noun. No unbounded quantity syntax.

rules.title: u10-fela-genitive
rules.rule: Invariant fela takes genitive plural for the selected many/count-group frame.
rules.boundary: Do not infer micel +mass or general noun-of-measure syntax.

rules.title: u10-governed-case-contrast
rules.rule: Choose case by the checked lexical frame: helpan+dative, geswīcan/gīeman+genitive, and new unnan/forwiernan+dative person+genitive thing.
rules.boundary: English object position does not decide Old English case; each lexical frame has separate evidence.

rules.title: u10-unnan-government
rules.rule: Unnan grants a genitive thing to a dative person.

rules.title: u10-forwiernan-government
rules.rule: Forwiernan refuses a genitive thing to a dative person.

rules.title: u10-dative-roles
rules.rule: Distinguish recipient, lexically governed person, beneficiary and experiencer. A shared dative form does not make the roles identical.
rules.boundary: Only separately documented lexical and prepositional frames are productive.

rules.title: u10-present-future
rules.rule: Present indicative can refer to future events where context supplies futurity; English will/shall need not produce willan.
rules.boundary: Willan remains volitional where intention is meant; no new periphrastic future tense.

rules.title: u10-to-destination
rules.rule: Tō+dative gives a destination with come/go/fly.
rules.boundary: Separate from tō purpose/function and tō+inflected infinitive.

rules.title: u10-on-side-idiom
rules.rule: Bounded on ... hand uses accusative in the right/left-hand expression, including attested static standan.
rules.boundary: Bare hand supports accusative; weak swīðran alone is case-ambiguous. Ordinary on+dative location remains available; Cook warns rest/motion distinction is not invariant.

rules.title: u10-on-name-idiom
rules.rule: Bounded on+genitive possessor+naman expresses in someone’s name; naman is dative and the internal possessor genitive.

rules.title: u10-beforan-location
rules.rule: Beforan+dative person expresses standing before/in front of someone.
rules.boundary: Explicit promotion of prior source-only exposure.

rules.title: u10-perception-object-predicate
rules.rule: Gesēon takes an accusative object with an agreeing accusative adjective describing its perceived condition.
rules.boundary: E.g. hungry/sick; do not convert it into the distinct accusative+infinitive frame.

rules.title: u10-hieran-perception-infinitive
rules.rule: Hīeran can take an accusative perceived actor with a plain infinitive naming its action.
rules.boundary: Explicit lexical extension distinct from prior gesēon frame; no general control/complement syntax.

rules.title: u10-substantival-personal-adjectives
rules.rule: The selected weak adjectives with the article can name people: the hungry, naked, sick, unrighteous; case and number follow their clause role.
rules.boundary: Plural people and an adjective modifying an expressed singular person must be distinguished. Do not imply every abstract substantive use is covered.

rules.title: u10-fedan-accusative-means
rules.rule: Fēdan takes accusative being fed; food may be expressed as mid+dative means or bounded bare instrumental means.
rules.boundary: Bare food example is new composition derived from independently checked lexical and case rules, not an exact quotation.

rules.title: u10-scrydan-accusative
rules.rule: Scrȳdan clothes an accusative person.
rules.boundary: Garment mid+dative is documented reference evidence only; it is not an additional independently assigned lexical complement.

rules.title: u10-andswarian-dative
rules.rule: Andswarian answers a dative addressee, with a following direct quotation if expressed.

rules.title: u10-scencan-recipient
rules.rule: Scęncan pours accusative drink for a dative recipient.

rules.title: u10-geneosian-accusative
rules.rule: Genēosian visits an accusative person in the selected frame.
rules.boundary: BT421 hine examples disambiguate accusative; nēosian genitive government is not denied.

rules.title: u10-gewitan-departure
rules.rule: Gewītan means depart/go away and may take fram+dative source.
rules.boundary: Not the distinct short-vowel preterite-present know.

rules.title: u10-togelaedan-recipient
rules.rule: Tōgelǣdan brings an accusative thing to a dative recipient.
rules.boundary: Promotes the actually supplied prior frame with full selected indicative morphology.

rules.title: u10-don-beneficiary
rules.rule: Dōn takes an accusative deed/it and dative affected person in the selected do-good-deeds-to frame.

rules.title: u10-totwaeman-separation
rules.rule: Tōtwǣman separates an accusative being/group from a fram+dative other group.
rules.boundary: Explicit lexical extension of prior division frame; no new verbal paradigm.

rules.title: u10-hwonne-direct-question
rules.rule: Hwonne introduces a direct when-question using ordinary finite interrogative syntax.
rules.boundary: No temporal subordinate when-clause system is introduced.

rules.title: u10-sellan-drink-infinitive
rules.rule: Supplied sęllan +dative person +plain drincan: give someone to drink.
rules.boundary: Local Cook III.14.11 support; not independent recall of a general purpose construction.

rules.title: u10-swa-lange-swa-supplied
rules.rule: Supplied swā lange swā ... expresses as long as / inasmuch as with the stated past actions.
rules.boundary: Supply both correlation tokens and lange. Cook p135 note17 explicitly observes inasmuch-as force; do not impose duration. No productive temporal-subordination system.

rules.title: u10-coordinated-predicate-ellipsis
rules.rule: In bounded coordination with two different expressed subjects, recover the omitted repeated predicate from the preceding clause.
rules.boundary: Cook III.15.9 morning/night coming; source p134 the angels share the preceding coming predicate. No free deletion rule.

rules.title: u10-wyrcean-work
rules.rule: Wyrcean takes accusative work/deed, including cognate weorc, in the selected work/perform sense.
rules.boundary: Distinguish this new ordinary sense from the earlier yield-fruit frame.

rules.title: u10-promoted-plain-infinitives
rules.rule: Promote the separately registered cīepan/bycgan plain infinitives for deliberate willan and blāwan for the new hīeran-perception construction.
rules.boundary: Only plain-infinitive use in these defined frames. Earlier supplied citation status is preserved historically.

rule_to_form_policy: Each derived form needs the relevant lexical evidence plus a morphology rule. A form shown in a paradigm does not acquire every syntactic use.
